logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

news.body: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake was reported 96 kilometers east-southeast of Isangel, Vanuatu, on September 8. According to the initial alert, the quake occurred.

logs.summary: A new magnitude 5.0 earthquake was recorded in the Vanuatu Islands on September 10, according to the GFZ German Research Centre, adding to the ongoing seismic sequence near Isangel following the initial September 5 event and the September 8 aftershock. Other reports mention a magnitude 5.2 quake off the Vanuatu coast and general increased activity in the Pacific Ring of Fire, but the September 10 quake is the most specific new update.

incidents.summary: A large wildfire on Croatia's Brač Island forced the evacuation of tourists, including dozens of Britons who fled into the sea to escape the flames. Around 700 people were evacuated by boat, and some swam to safety, with the fire being described as highly dangerous and unpredictable. The incident prompted travel advice updates for the region.
